ratings_why.fun: Line order as the puzzle is a good climb, but early turns are thin (Breeder Pups clog hand) and the Front and Tide halves often undercut each other mid-game.
ratings_why.distinct: A Lead title that moves, with Onward and Takes the lead as mirror triggers and Front Lemming rotating it, plays unlike any current tribe, though the Tide half is a familiar token-and-death tribe.

verdict_why: The Lead rules don't say how Front Lemming's rotation squares with "first living unit" and summons taking the lead, which the whole Front build rests on.

points.text: Front Lemming conflicts with the Lead rule: after it rotates the lead to a back unit, does a death or a Pup summoned in F1 snap the lead back to the first unit, or pass to the next? State one rule.
Lemenar Herald's halving needs a reading: with two Heralds, or after The One Who Arrived buffs Pups, which bonus halves, and do Pups already on board lose stats?
Turns 1-4 rest on two T1s and a Breeder whose Pups take hand space; a T2 that fights well on its own (a body that grows when it takes the lead in the shop phase) would smooth the early climb.
Snow-Hall Midwife locks out every Takes-the-lead unit; letting its Pup go to the nearest empty slot instead of the Lead's slot would let the two halves share a board without losing the Tide's refill.
Brother Onward is the build-defining T5, but it pays most with Pup deaths into a real Lead; a line on screen showing who will keep the permanent stats would make the choice readable.

standouts.why: Cliff-Singer turns the doom cult into a real enabler: kill a fat Lead, an Ooze or a Nest Mother on purpose and keep the value.
Front Lemming makes the lead lap the board, turning Banner-Bearer, Gerd and Rune-Carver into repeat triggers: a fresh late-game engine.
The One Who Arrived turns a bloody fight into permanent herd growth, a clean late-game payoff with a natural brake.

weakest.why: Weeks-Old Breeder adds a 1/1 to a 4-card hand each turn; weak tempo unless Tally or triples are online.
Herding Councillor's per-neighbour count is small and awkward next to a Lead in F1, which has few neighbours.
Banner-Bearer is a vanilla 1/3 until Front Lemming or Cliff-Singer make it lead more than once.

flags.note: Golden Rune-Carver with Front Lemming pays every lap per death so far; fight-only, but a big spike.
Tally plus Breeder plus Pup triples gives gold and tier-up Discovers every few turns; could outpace other tribes' economy.
Brother Onward with Midwife and Ole feeding Pup Onwards into a real Lead makes one permanent giant fast; fine to run hot, owner's eye.
Rotation versus "first living unit" and summons taking the lead is not settled.
